instructions.question: Does the tweet carry an upbeat evaluation, a critical or unhappy one, or no clear evaluation?
instructions.rule: Polar labels need clear evaluative wording. Positive needs the author's own warmth or praise (good, love, can't wait, :) or <3 aimed at something) or clearly good news. Negative needs explicit negative judgment (hypocritical, bitter, worst, sucks) or real distress, or harmful news. Neutral covers: tactical sports second-guessing and game recaps, argumentative political or religious replies, small inconveniences told lightly, event ads ('don't miss', 'check out', 'place to be'), plans, joking or nostalgic banter, arrest or court news.

neutral.what: Information, ads, plans, questions, banter, tactical opinions, political or religious debate replies, mild inconveniences.
examples: David Price should not have been pitching in the 8th. They can't get a 6-outs from the bullpen? Yankees - Jays
@user You do realize that the 1st Amendment doesn't just apply to Christians, right?"
I could be going to digi tomorrow but I thought I was supposed to be seeing the girls but they cancelled lmao
neutral.cues: should have, why, c'mon, you do realize, still waiting, lmao, don't miss, check out, who's going, hoping
neutral.not_for: Explicit insults or harsh judgment words are negative; personal praise or excitement is positive.

positive.what: The author's own excitement, affection, praise or hope, warm sales pitches with praise words, or clear good news or achievements.
examples: Jason Aldean&Kenny Chesney tickets for sale. Concert is the 29th. Good seats for a really good price. Text me asap for more info!!
We always mess up when we get the chance to go up the table when Atleti or Barca mess up. PLEASE WIN TOMORROW :) @user
positive.cues: good, best, love, can't wait, so excited, perfect, :), <3, congrats, record, Happy [day]
positive.not_for: Event ads with only 'don't miss' or 'check out', plain plans, jokes and nostalgia are neutral.

negative.what: Explicit criticism or contempt, real frustration or sadness, sarcasm, or news of violence or harm.
examples: "Caitlyn Jenner may not be ""down"" with gay marriage, but she should really understand that people are gonna see that as hypocritical."
@user I used to really like Rick Perry, just has become so bitter. He may be very sad. He should try to smile
A Thursday night with no Waterloo road on! #boring
negative.cues: hypocritical, bitter, flop, racist, worst, sucks, argh, #boring, #not, damn, attack, dead
negative.not_for: Second-guessing, debate replies and minor hassles are neutral; strong words used in excitement are positive.
